title: A run that stops while the client is still refused a login ends the client instead of asking it to quit
notes: This scenario is meant to fail, and it fails on the one state a client must never be asked to quit in.
A client that has been refused a login opens a page of KingsIsle's in the machine's own browser the
moment it is asked to quit. Measured on 2026-09-18: pressing the dialog away does not help, and neither
does waiting for the login window to come back, because the state outlasts both; a client admitted since
the refusal does not do it. references.json carries that as a rule over the client's own log, and this
scenario is what holds the teardown to it: the run fails, the client is ended rather than asked to quit,
and the report's line about the client opening nothing outside itself still passes.

steps.name: the client brings its renderer up
the login window is on the screen
the client is told the login failed
the invalid-login dialog is on the screen
the screen the run stops on
a line the client will never write
